This bundle performs no record write of its own: no row insert, no retirement move, no staged-entry flush. Its deliverable is the verified end state the performed work produced: the eight historical payment rows (C-CONTRACT-DEBT, C-RECORDED-DEBT, C-SUBSTANTIATION-HONESTY, C-REPORT-HONESTY, C-FLAG-HONESTY, C-ESCALATION-HONESTY, C-RECOVER-FOLDABLE, C-EXECUTION-CONTRACT) retired as kind="historical" in registry-retired.xml and absent from live registry.xml; the nineteen findings they pay retired in findings-retired.xml with stamped PaidBy naming their payer; F204 flushed and live in findings.xml and decisions.xml; every live root consistent with its persisted ceiling and with the shipped counting metrics; every ceiling byte-identical to the base commit; a second --retire a byte-level no-op. The writes were performed under the superseded bundle C-PAYMENT-RECORD-3 — archived at .ngrace/changes/archive/C-PAYMENT-RECORD-3/ with spec and plan status="superseded" and a <Replacement>C-PAYMENT-RECORD-4</Replacement> pointer — and those archived artifacts are the durable record of what was planned and executed; this bundle asserts the state they produced and adds no write to it. One reconciliation is in scope because the performed work collided with two shipped tests that pin the record's pre-payment state: bun test is red on this branch in exactly two tests (measured at this commit), the C-RECORD-PARSE payer-derivation production probe and the artifact element-span count pin, and this bundle's close evidence runs that suite. The plan's first task reconciles those pins to the measured post-payment state and adds three discriminating production assertions to the suite file it already writes; no record file is written. C-PAYMENT-RECORD-4.Problem:
A copy of the superseded spec would be unsatisfiable, and that is the whole design problem. C-PAYMENT-RECORD-3's criteria asserted a transition — the intermediate state reporting 8 registry-eligibility findings plus 19 finding-eligibility findings, --retire reporting moved = 27 — that its own execution consumed: measured on this branch, zero of the eight rows and zero of the nineteen tokens remain live, and --retire reports moved = 0. Those criteria can never be observed again, by this bundle or any other. Its AC-NO-SRC went stale differently: it pinned src/ and scripts/ byte-identical to 49b4ebb, and C-RECORD-PARSE — merged into main at this bundle's fork point — changed 24 files there before this bundle existed (measured: git diff --name-only 49b4ebb..fork over src/ scripts/ = 24). Neither criterion was wrong when written; each pinned a fact that stopped being true for reasons outside the bundle. That is the failure mode this spec is written to avoid.
The authority's design, adopted here after measuring both directions: assert the end state rather than the transition. The end state is auditable — the archived predecessor carries the spec and plan of what was executed, its run-ledger carries the execution events, and this bundle's criteria re-derive the state from the record files with commands that discriminate. The alternative, re-performing the writes, is not available: re-running the row insert would duplicate rows the retired layer already holds, and the move has nothing left to move (measured: --retire on a copy of this record reports moved = 0 and leaves all seven record files byte-identical).
Verifying that state honestly surfaced one more cost of the performed work: two shipped tests pinned the record's pre-payment shape and are now red. The scripts/fixtures/record-parse/baseline-probes.json payer baseline was captured at 49b4ebb with 56 tokens, and none of the nineteen row-derived tokens is in it (measured), so the payer-derivation production probe fails its second direction; and src/artifact/xml.test.ts pins the production element counts (213 live findings, 337 index entries among them) that the move and the flush legitimately changed (measured: 195/77/44/338). validate:ci runs bun run test, so the branch is CI-red today through no fault of its record — the pins, not the record, are stale. No debt is carried forward: this bundle charters the reconciliation as its own task rather than leaving a red suite behind an unclosable verify bundle, which would repeat the failure shape that superseded the predecessor.

Ceilings, one-shot: every persisted ceiling is byte-identical to its value at the base commit — ceilings are rewritten only by a move and never raised, so the post-payment roots must carry the ceiling attributes the pre-payment record carried. That comparison stays out of the suite, because a base commit hard-coded into a test is exactly the staleness this bundle is paying off, and is measured by the second Command below: a git diff --exit-code --no-index over the ceiling attributes extracted from the root line of git show at the base commit and from the working root lines, four per file, in a throwaway directory.
